callouts.title: Fubini-Tonelli定理
callouts.body:

Y}f(x,y)\,d(\mu\times\nu) = \int_{X}\left(\int_Y f(x,y) \,
d\nu\right) \, d\mu = \int_Y\left(\int_X f(x,y) \,
d\mu\right) \, d\nu$$

callouts.title: Fubini-Tonelli定理的一个使用策略
callouts.body:
注意到，Tonelli定理只需要要求非负函数是可测函数，并不要求可积。因此有这样的策略:

1.  首先使用Tonelli定理计算$|f|$的积分，如果可测的话。如果一切顺利，那么积分是有限的，于是Fubini定理自然成立。
2.  如果发现其中一个积分计算出来是无穷的情况，那么自然证明原来的函数$f$并不可积，于是Fubini定理失效。

classification_result.english_title: A Strategy for Using the Fubini-Tonelli Theorem

if_strategy_template.strategy_name_en: Check absolute integrability via Tonelli first
if_strategy_template.summary_en: First apply Tonelli's theorem to $|f|$ when it is measurable. If the resulting integral is finite, then $f$ is integrable and Fubini applies; if it is infinite, then $f$ is not integrable and Fubini fails.
if_strategy_template.applicability: Use this when deciding whether an interchange of order of integration is justified for a possibly signed measurable function.

callouts.title: 想法1.1
callouts.body:
**无需依赖几何图像**，先把积分写成一个标准的$\mathbb{R}^n$或者某个超立方体上的积分，积分区域用条件函数$1_{\text{条件}}$来确定，将几何边界转换为不等式组。然后再根据积分的特性，选择合适的累次积分，从而实现对积分的化简。

---

1. 一种化简的思路是：被积函数$f(x,*)$本身并没有好的原函数，然而如果我们可以通过交换次序，把难积的变量$x$置于外层，想办法在内层的积分中，制造一个$g(x)$，满足$f(x,*)g(x)$有很好的原函数，那么这样外层积分就能变得容易写出简单形式。

if_strategy_template.strategy_name_en: Rewrite as a standard multiple integral and choose the order strategically
if_strategy_template.summary_en: Avoid relying on geometric pictures by rewriting the region as an integral over $\mathbb{R}^n$ or a box with an indicator function. Then choose the order of integration to create an inner integral or multiplicative factor that simplifies the remaining outer integral.
if_strategy_template.applicability: Use this for multiple integrals over complicated regions, especially when one order of integration has no convenient antiderivative but another order produces a tractable expression.

callouts.title: 例子1.2

if_problem.statement_en:
Let $f$ be integrable on the closed interval $[0,b]$, and define
$$g(x)=\int_{x}^{b}\frac{f(t)}{t}dt,\quad 0 <x\leq b.$$ Prove that $g$ is integrable on $(0,b]$ and that
$$\int_{0}^{b}g(x)dx = \int_{0}^{b}f(t)dt.$$
key_techniques: integral representation over a triangular region
prerequisites: Riemann or Lebesgue integrability on intervals

callouts.title: 例子1.3
callouts.body:
计算积分$$I:=\int_0^1 \,dx \int_x^1 \,dy \int_0^1 \,e^{y^2}\,dz$$这个累次积分，如果我们按照正常的次序进行下去，就会发现第二层$y$变量的积分，由于$e^{y^2}$的存在从而没有初等原函数。但倘若我们可以制造一个$ye^{y^2}$那么整个积分就会简单许多。

我们先把$I$通过条件函数写成$[0,1]^3$上的积分$$I:=\iiint_{[0,1]^3}e^{y^2}\cdot 1_{x\leq y\leq 1}\,dx\,dy\,dz$$然后我们把$y$置于最外层，整个积分按照从外到内为$y-x-z$的形式写成累次积分,于是$$I=\int_0^1 e^{y^2}\int_0^y\,dx\int_0^1 1\,dz=\int_0^1 ye^{y^2}\,dy=\frac{e-1}{2}$$

if_problem.statement_en:
Compute the iterated integral
$$I:=\int_0^1 \,dx \int_x^1 \,dy \int_0^1 \,e^{y^2}\,dz.$$ The direct order leads to the non-elementary antiderivative of $e^{y^2}$, so the integral should be rewritten over $[0,1]^3$ using an indicator function and evaluated by changing the order of integration.

callouts.title: 反例2.1: 函数不可积导致Fubini定理失效
callouts.body:
$$f(x,y):=\begin{cases}\frac{x^2-y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^{2}}&(x,y)\in[0,1]^2,(x,y)\not = (0,0)\\0 &(x,y)=(0,0)\end{cases}$$令$I = [0,1]$，首先函数$|f|$是可测的，因此由Tonelli定理直接交换顺序计算(如果发现不可积，可以稍微放缩):$$\begin{aligned}\int_{I^2}|f(x,y)|d(x,y)&=\int_{I^2}
\frac{x^2-y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^{2}}1_{\{1>x\geq
y>0\}}d(x,y)+\int_{I^2}\frac{y^2-x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^{2}}1_{\{0<x<y\leq1\}}d(x,y)\\
&\geq\int_{0}^{1}\int_{0}^{x}\frac{x^2-y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^{2}}dydx
= \int_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2x}dx = +\infty
\end{aligned}$$因此这个例子当中Fubini定理是不可用的。实际上使用Fubini定理会发现:

1.  $\int_0^1 \left(\int_0^1 \frac{x^2-y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2} dy\right) dx = \int_0^1 \frac{1}{1+x^2} dx = \frac{\pi}{4}$
2.  $\int_0^1 \left(\int_0^1 \frac{x^2-y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2} dx\right) dy = - \frac{\pi}{4}$

classification_result.english_title: Counterexample 2.1: Failure of Fubini Caused by Non-Integrability

if_problem.statement_en:
Consider
$$f(x,y):=\begin{cases}\frac{x^2-y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^{2}}&(x,y)\in[0,1]^2,(x,y)\not = (0,0)\\0 &(x,y)=(0,0).\end{cases}$$
Let $I = [0,1]$. Show that $|f|$ is measurable but
$$\int_{I^2}|f(x,y)|d(x,y)=+\infty,$$
so $f$ is not integrable and Fubini's theorem does not apply. Moreover, the two iterated integrals give different values:
$$\int_0^1 \left(\int_0^1 \frac{x^2-y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2} dy\right) dx = \frac{\pi}{4},$$
while
$$\int_0^1 \left(\int_0^1 \frac{x^2-y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2} dx\right) dy = - \frac{\pi}{4}.$$
key_techniques: lower bound comparison to a divergent integral

callouts.title: 反例2.2: $\sigma-\text{finite}$条件缺失导致失效
callouts.body:
$I =[0,1]$然后令$\mathcal{B}(I)$是Borel代数，令$\mu$是Lebesgue测度，$\nu$是counting measure,现在构建两个测度空间:$(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\mu)$以及$(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\nu)$.

考虑$I^2$当中的一个闭集$D=\{(x,y):x=y,(x,y)\in I^2\}$,那么自然$D\in \mathcal{B}(I^2) = \mathcal{B}(I) \otimes \mathcal{B}(I) \subset \mathcal{B}(I) \otimes \mathcal{P}(I)$现在考虑计算积分
$$\int_{I^2}1_{D} d(\mu \times \nu)$$

1.  $\int_{I}\left(\int_{I} 1_{D}(x,y) d\mu(x)\right)d\nu(y)=\int_{I}0d\nu(y)=0$
2.  $\int_{I}\left(\int_{I} 1_{D}(x,y) d\nu(y)\right)d\mu(x)=\int_{I}1d\mu(x)=1$

这主要是因为$\nu$是counting measure，所以$(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\nu)$并不是$\sigma-\text{finite}$的测度空间.

classification_result.english_title: Counterexample 2.2: Failure Caused by the Absence of the $\sigma$-Finite Condition

if_problem.statement_en:
Let $I =[0,1]$, let $\mathcal{B}(I)$ be the Borel algebra, let $\mu$ be Lebesgue measure, and let $\nu$ be counting measure. Consider the measure spaces $(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\mu)$ and $(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\nu)$. For the diagonal set
$$D=\{(x,y):x=y,(x,y)\in I^2\},$$
compute
$$\int_{I^2}1_{D} \, d(\mu \times \nu).$$
Then show that
$$\int_{I}\left(\int_{I} 1_{D}(x,y) \, d\mu(x)\right)d\nu(y)=0,$$
whereas
$$\int_{I}\left(\int_{I} 1_{D}(x,y) \, d\nu(y)\right)d\mu(x)=1,$$
and explain that the failure comes from the fact that $(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\nu)$ is not $\sigma$-finite.
key_techniques: diagonal set in a product space

callouts.title: 反例2.3:不可积的例子2
callouts.body:
$$f(x,y):=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{y^2}&0<x<y<1\\
-\frac{1}{x^2}&0<y<x<1 \\ 0 &\text{ otherwise}\end{cases}$$
先考虑Tonelli定理,$I=[0,1]$,$$\begin{aligned}\int_I\int_I
|f(x,y)|\,dydx&=\int_I\int_I
\frac{1}{y^2}1_{\{0<x<y<1\}}\,dydx + \int_I\int_I
\frac{1}{x^2}1_{\{0<y<x<1\}}\,dydx\\&=
\int_{0}^{1}\int_{x}^{1}\frac{1}{y^2}\,dydx+
\int_{0}^{1}\int_{0}^{x} \frac{1}{x^2}\,dydx \\ &\ge
\int_{0}^{1}\int_{x}^{1}\frac{1}{y^2}\,dydx
=\int_{0}^{1}(-1+1/x)\,dx =
+\infty\end{aligned}$$因此显然，函数并不可积，所以Fubini定理是不适用的，因此可以很容易预期：
$$\int_I\int_I f(x,y)dydx \neq \int_I\int_I f(x,y)dxdy $$

if_problem.statement_en:
Consider
$$f(x,y):=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{y^2}&0<x<y<1\\
-\frac{1}{x^2}&0<y<x<1 \\ 0 &\text{ otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
Let $I=[0,1]$. Show first that
$$\int_I\int_I |f(x,y)|\,dydx=+\infty,$$
so $f$ is not integrable and Fubini's theorem does not apply. Conclude that one should expect
$$\int_I\int_I f(x,y)dydx \neq \int_I\int_I f(x,y)dxdy.$$
key_techniques: Tonelli theorem on the absolute value

callouts.title: 反例2.4: 和的版本的反例
callouts.body:
$\Omega=\{\ 1,2,3,.....\}$，$\mu$是counting measure，$\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$是幂集。这样可以建立一个可测空$(\Omega,\mathcal{P}(\Omega),\mu)$，然后在$\mathcal{P}(\Omega)\otimes \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$上定义测度$\mu\times \mu$，现在考虑在$\Omega^2$上对函数的积分:
$$f(i,j)=\begin{cases}1&\text{ if }i=j \\ -1&\text{ if }i=j+1\\ 0&\text{ otherwise}\end{cases}$$我们可以把$\Omega^2$看成是一个无限阶的矩阵，那么函数的取值写成矩阵就是:
$$[f(i,j)]=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0&0&\cdots\\ -1&1&0&0&\cdots\\0&-1&1&0&\cdots\\0&0&-1&1&\cdots\\ \vdots&\vdots&0&-1&\cdots\\ \vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots \\0&0&0&0&\cdots\end{bmatrix}$$也就是说考虑积分:
$$\int_{\Omega^2}f(i,j)d(\mu\times \mu) =\sum_{i,j\in\Omega}f(i,j)$$也就是说这实际上就是求和。

这个积分实际上是不积的，因为$\sum_{i,j\in\Omega}|f(i,j)|$实际上并不收敛。这意味着Fubini定理在此处是不适用的，如果一定要尝试，会发现累次积分不一致:

1.  $\int\left(\int f(x,y)\,d\mu(y)\right)d\mu(x)=\sum_{i=1}^\infty \left(\sum_{j=1}^\infty f(i,j)\right)=1$
2.  $\int\left(\int f(x,y)\,d\mu(x)\right)d\mu(y)=\sum_{j=1}^\infty\left(\sum_{i=1}^\infty f(i,j)\right)=0$

classification_result.english_title: Counterexample 2.4: Counterexample in the Summation Version

if_problem.statement_en:
Let $\Omega=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$, let $\mu$ be counting measure, and let $\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ be the power set. Define on $\Omega^2$ the function
$$f(i,j)=\begin{cases}1&\text{ if }i=j \\ -1&\text{ if }i=j+1\\ 0&\text{ otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
Interpret
$$\int_{\Omega^2}f(i,j)d(\mu\times \mu) =\sum_{i,j\in\Omega}f(i,j),$$
and show that this is not absolutely summable because
$$\sum_{i,j\in\Omega}|f(i,j)|$$
diverges. Therefore Fubini's theorem does not apply, and the two iterated sums differ:
$$\sum_{i=1}^\infty \left(\sum_{j=1}^\infty f(i,j)\right)=1,$$
while
$$\sum_{j=1}^\infty\left(\sum_{i=1}^\infty f(i,j)\right)=0.$$
key_techniques: comparison of row and column sums
